newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury to pay down $65 bln in Q2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury to pay down $65 bln in Q2.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Monday its net market borrowing in the April-June second quarter will result in a debt paydown of $65 billion, assuming a cash balance of $35 billion on June 30.

That means Treasury will issue marketable securities in the quarter that will be about $65 billion less than the total of maturing securities in the same period, thus reducing the government's accumulated debt.
Treasury said its actual net borrowing in the first quarter that ended March 31 was $44.6 billion, with an end-of-quarter cash balance of $33.5 billion.
Treasury also said it estimated its net market borrowing need in the July-September third quarter will be in the range of $40 billion to $45 billion with a cash balance of $40 bilion on Sept 30.
Treasury has scheduled a news conference for Wednesday, April 30, to detail its plans for selling three- and 10-year notes next week to meet its financing needs for the second quarter.

Treasury noted that, on Feb 3, it estimated its borrowing in the second quarter would result in a smaller paydown of $10 billion to $15 billion with a cash balance of $35 billion on June 30 and that it had expected to have a larger net borrowing need in the first quarter of $50 billion with a $20 billion cash balance on March 31.
"The combined improvement of $19 billion was the result of higher than estimated receipts and lower than estimated outlays," Treasury said.

Treasury has a larger tax take in the second quarter because it includes the April 15 deadline for filing personal income tax returns for the prior year, creating the opportunity for Treasury to pay down rather than run up the national debt.
